config.title: Majority Element

intro.title: Majority Element
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that finds the majority element in an array, which is the element that appears more than half the time. You will learn the core concept of frequency counting using a hash map to track occurrences efficiently. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, objects for mapping, and conditional logic. This beginner-friendly exercise will help you practice problem-solving with common data structures and algorithms.
intro.usecase: The majority element algorithm is essential in systems that analyze user behavior or aggregate preferences, such as social media platforms identifying trending hashtags or e-commerce sites determining most popular products. In developer tools, it helps analyze log files to find the most frequent error type across thousands of requests. This pattern also powers recommendation engines that need to identify dominant user preferences from large datasets, and voting systems that must quickly determine if a candidate has majority support in real-time results.

objectives: Implement the Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm to find the majority element in an array
Initialize and manipulate a candidate variable and counter to track potential majority elements
Apply conditional logic to update the candidate and counter while iterating through the array
Configure a final verification step to confirm the candidate appears more than n/2 times
Construct a function that returns the majority element or indicates when none exists
Integrate the algorithm into a complete solution that handles various input arrays

content.body: Have you ever wondered how to find the most common element in a list? In this lesson, we'll learn how to identify the majority element—the value that appears more than half the time. This is a common pattern in data analysis and voting systems.
content.title: Welcome

content.body:
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Explain what a majority element is and why it matters
2. Apply a hash map to track element frequencies efficiently
3. Implement an algorithm that finds the majority element in one pass
4. Determine when to check the hash map versus add to it
5. Choose appropriate keys and values for frequency tracking
content.title: What you'll learn
Try it
content.prompt: Look at this small array: [3, 2, 3]. Which number appears most frequently?
content.successMessage: Correct! The number 3 appears twice, which is more than half the array length.

content.title: Try a bigger array
content.prompt: Now look at [2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2]. Which number appears more than half the time?
content.successMessage: Well done! The number 2 appears four times out of seven, which is more than half.

content.title: One more
content.prompt: What about [1, 3, 3, 4, 3, 2, 3, 3, 5, 3]? Find the majority element.
content.successMessage: Great! You found that 3 appears six times out of ten—that's the majority element.

content.body: What you just did was manually count each element's occurrences by scanning through the array. For small arrays, this works fine, but it requires you to keep track of counts in your head as you go.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When arrays have thousands of elements, manually counting becomes impossible. We need a systematic way to track frequencies without losing count. Can't figure out how? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: The solution is to remember what we have already seen. Think of it like keeping a notebook where you write down each number and how many times you've encountered it. Instead of rescanning the entire array for each element, you check your notebook in one step.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: A notebook where we write down what we've seen and check it in one step.

content.body: We'll use a hash map (JavaScript object) as our notebook. As we go through the array, we'll check if we've seen the current number before. If we have, we increase its count. If not, we add it to our notebook. We'll also track the current majority candidate.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Walkthrough with [3, 2, 3]:
1. Start with empty notebook and no majority
2. See 3 → not in notebook → add {3:1}, majority=3
3. See 2 → not in notebook → add {3:1, 2:1}, majority still 3
4. See 3 → in notebook → update {3:2, 2:1}, count(3)=2 > n/2 → 3 is majority

content.body:
1. Create an empty object to store frequencies
2. Initialize variables for majority element and its count
3. Loop through each element in the array
4. For each element:
   - If it's not in the frequency object, add it with count 1
   - If it is in the object, increment its count
   - Update the majority if this element's count is higher
5. After the loop, verify the majority element appears > n/2 times
6. Return the majority element
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Create the function skeleton
steps.instruction: Start by creating a function called majorityElement that takes one parameter: nums (the array). Return 0 for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function declaration with correct name and parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the function structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost! Make sure the function name is exactly 'majorityElement' and it takes 'nums' as parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called majorityElement that accepts nums.

steps.title: Initialize tracking variables
steps.instruction: Inside the function, create two variables: 'counts' as an empty object to store frequencies, and 'majority' set to null. Also create 'maxCount' set to 0.
steps.hint: let counts = {}; let majority = null; let maxCount = 0;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've set up the tracking variables we need.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close! Make sure you have 'counts' as empty object, 'majority' as null, and 'maxCount' as 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: we need an object for counts, null for majority, and 0 for maxCount.

steps.title: Create the loop structure
steps.instruction: Add a for loop that iterates through each element in nums. Use 'let i = 0' as the starting point.
steps.expectedOutcome: For loop that iterates through nums array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! The loop will process each element one by one.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there! Check your loop syntax - it should go from i=0 to i<nums.length.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need a for loop that goes through all elements in nums.

steps.title: Check and update frequencies
steps.instruction: Inside the loop, get the current number: 'let num = nums[i]'. Then check if it exists in counts. If not, add it with count 1. If it does exist, increment its count.
steps.expectedOutcome: Frequency tracking logic inside the loop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Now we're remembering what we've seen by updating counts.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're checking if the number exists in counts, then either setting to 1 or incrementing.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: we need to check if the number is in counts, then update accordingly.

steps.title: Track the current majority
steps.instruction: After updating the count for the current number, check if its count is greater than maxCount. If it is, update maxCount and set majority to this number.
steps.hint: if (counts[num] > maxCount) { maxCount = counts[num]; majority = num; }
steps.expectedOutcome: Majority tracking logic after count update
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Now we're keeping track of which element has the highest count so far.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost! Check that you're comparing counts[num] with maxCount and updating both variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to check if the current number's count exceeds maxCount, then update both maxCount and majority.

steps.title: Return the result
steps.instruction: After the loop ends, return the majority element. Also add a check to verify it's truly the majority (appears more than n/2 times).
steps.hint: if (maxCount > nums.length / 2) { return majority; } return null;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You've implemented the complete majority element algorithm.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good! Make sure you're checking if maxCount > nums.length/2 before returning majority.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to verify the majority appears more than half the time before returning it.

content.body: Congratulations! You've successfully implemented the majority element algorithm using a hash map. Remember: the key insight is to remember what we've already seen by using a lookup structure. Store elements as keys and their counts as values. Check the structure before adding to it to avoid duplicate entries. This approach lets us find the majority in a single pass through the array—much more efficient than checking every pair!
content.title: Done
